newsitem.title: FRANCE: AGF shares slump on interest in GAN.
newsitem.headline: AGF shares slump on interest in GAN.

text.p: Shares in France's second largest insurer, AGF, fell more than three percent on Friday on worries it was setting its sights on troubled rival GAN to boost its market clout following the Axa-UAP mega-merger, analyst said.
"There is concern over whether management would be capable of handling an acquisition like that," said a London analyst. "It doesn't have the experience in takeovers of the Axa team."

On Thursday, AGF, reporting 1996 profits rose 42 percent to 1.54 billion francs ($267.8 million), said the group was mulling an acquisition to strengthen its market position -- and suggested it could be state-controlled Groupe des Assurances Nationales or the smaller Athena insurance group.

Chairman Antoine Jeancourt-Galignani said AGF, itself privatised last year, needed to know more about the terms of the sale of GAN before deciding whether to bid but added GAN had activities that "complement our own".
AGF's stock closed down 3.03 percent at 208 francs with 1.1 million shares traded.

The government plans to pump 20 billion francs into GAN, forced to take repeated provisions to cover property losses, to ready it for sale this year. But "there is the worry with GAN you never quite know what will be in there," said one analyst.
At least one investment house downgraded the share. Paris brokerage Dupont Denant cut its recommendation on the AGF share to hold from buy, citing the prospect of AGF acquisitions.

Also hitting the shares, analysts said, were fading hopes that AGF itself would be a takeover target. AGF has been at the centre of speculation in the past few weeks that it could be the subject of a bid, notably by Allianz of Germany.

But AGF has always argued a bid by Allianz would encounter problems with competition authorities. And Allianz said this week it was looking at GAN. "The balance has swung from AGF being taken over to it taking over something," said an analyst.

Jeancourt-Galignani underlined on Thursday AGF's aim to stay independent and said any bid for AGF would be hostile and costly in light of the recent jump in its share price. One person close to AGF estimated the cost of a takeover at 35-40 billion francs.

AGF, meanwhile, denied on Friday a article in the weekly magazine Nouvel Economiste claiming it had asked bank Societe Generale and holding firm Paribas to buy up its shares to thwart any takeover bid.
AGF's profits were in line with expectations, analysts said, but some expressed surprise at the size of capital gains as well as at losses from its British operations and banking activities.

The UK operations, hit by a collapse in car insurance premium prices, swung to a loss of 273 million francs from a profit of 81 million francs. Banking losses swelled to 526 million from losses of 490 million the previous year.
"People are worried about whether it is the best way forward for this company with weak earnings in terms of quality to think about growing bigger," one analyst said. ($ = 5.75 French Francs)
